To unblock the remaining WSL rows, the owner needs to decide: (1) whether to allow creating a disposable second WSL distribution (wsl --import) and running wsl --terminate on it, for P-B08 multi-distribution, P-B09 restart and P-B10 idle; (2) whether someone will be at the console for P-B07 host lock and for the P-A06 'no UAC prompt' attestation; (3) whether a second Linux account with non-interactive sudo may be created, for the P-B01 other-user rows; (4) whether a second Windows account may be created, for P-B11.

summary:
I ran the G03 WSL harness for the first time in the owner's WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04.5 (WSL 3.0.1, networking mode nat, appendWindowsPath=false). It ran in a wsl.exe-launched session, with the Windows fixture agent from Invoke-G03WindowsProbes.ps1 -ServeAgentForWsl (pwsh 7.6.6, fixture and decoy pipe names only). The WSLENV SSH_AUTH_SOCK/w echo gate passed before any ssh.exe run, and the decoy saw no connection in any of the three runs.

Definitive run r2, promoted into tests/evidence/g03-wsl-*.json:
- verified/pass (11): env-inventory, a-executable-selection, a-process-io, a-path-quoting, a-git, a-cert-change, b-unauthorized-key, b-relay-attribution, b-socket-deletion, b-stale-socket, b-teardown-deadline.
- in_progress/inconclusive (2): a-elevation (child observed not elevated; the UAC attestation needs an operator) and b-endpoint-perms (the other-Linux-user row needs a second account).
- blocked (4): b-host-lock (operator) and the lifecycle probes multi, restart and idle. Those need a disposable second distribution and wsl --terminate, which were not authorized; they were not run.

Supplementary run r3 repeated the Mode A probes with the MSI ssh.exe 10.0p2, with identical results. Debug run r1 failed only the certificate rows, because the fixture port fell in a Windows excluded port range (fixture problem, then fixed).

Four harness defects were fixed with minimal changes, logged in tests/native/wsl/CHANGELOG-native.md; no criterion was weakened:
1. Windows tools were not on PATH.
2. Endpoint directories under XDG_RUNTIME_DIR were left behind.
3. Redaction lacked the <wsluser>/<winuser>/<winhost>/<wslhome>/<winhome> tokens.
4. whoami /groups leaked a Microsoft-account e-mail address; only the label row is kept now, plus e-mail redaction.

Doc changes: the §0 WSL rows are updated, and the new §0.2 covers the run plus how Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Cursor and OpenCode would start ssh inside WSL. All of them would use Linux /usr/bin/ssh with an inherited environment; Codex and OpenCode use login shells; the Claude Code, Codex and Cursor sandboxes block plain ssh TCP and possibly AF_UNIX; Pi and OpenCode have no sandbox.

All host processes, pipes, sshd fixtures and scratch were removed (verified). No commit was made.
